title: Cofinal restriction of relative join cocones and its dual
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], join slices of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], and inner fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $j:A\hookrightarrow B$ be a full subcategory of a small quasicategory, and suppose that for each $b\in B$ the coherent comma quasicategory of arrows $b\to j(a)$ is weakly contractible. Let $p:C\to D$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories and $u:B\to C$ a functor. Define $(C_{u/})_k$ to consist of maps $B\star\Delta^k\to C$ restricting to $u$, with restriction operators, and analogously for the other coslices. Then
$$C_{u/}\longrightarrow C_{uj/}\times_{D_{puj/}}D_{pu/}$$
is a trivial Kan fibration, so every prescribed boundary and every prescribed base simplex lift exactly. The hypothesis holds in particular if the inclusion $j$ admits a left adjoint, meaning a coherent functor $R:B\to A$ with coherently natural equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_A(Rb,a)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_B(b,j a)$. Dually, if each comma quasicategory of arrows $j(a)\to b$ is weakly contractible, restriction induces a trivial Kan fibration
$$C_{/u}\longrightarrow C_{/uj}\times_{D_{/puj}}D_{/pu}.$$
The dual hypothesis holds when $A$ chooses one initial object in each component of $B$. Weak contractibility means weak homotopy equivalence to a point; a trivial Kan fibration lifts every boundary inclusion, including dimension zero. There are no colimit or limit existence assumptions.
